To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The olfactory bulb is a model system for the study of the neural mechanisms of learning and memory.

(1) the neocortex, a phylogenetically recent brain structure, is the principal site for processing sensory and motor information, and that (2) the neocortical circuitry has evolved to perform computations that enable the brain to store and retrieve memories.

(1) the olfactory bulb is an ideal model system for the investigation of synaptic plasticity and memory, and (2) olfactory bulb synapses exhibit a wide range of plasticity mechanisms, including both Hebbian and non-Hebbian plasticity, which can interact to produce complex forms of associative plasticity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying learning and memory, and with the neural systems that underlie the storage and retrieval of information.
the neural mechanisms underlying learning, memory and recognition.
the mechanisms and functions of synaptic modifications, and how the brain’s circuit architecture supports memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the olfactory system is the best model to study the telencephalon and the mammalian brain.
the mammalian brain is organized in a way that is fundamentally different than the brains of other vertebrates.
the mammalian neopallium is the most important brain structure in terms of memory and learning, and the neocortex is the most important structure in the neopallium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are trying to figure out how the neocortex works.

we have shown how a cortical circuit architecture, with the synaptic modifications of its neurons, can give rise to a wide variety of memory functions, including recognition and recall, and how interactions among such circuits give rise to still more memory functions.
we are studying how a matrix is transformed into a map.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain has a lot of memory.
the neocortex is a highly parallel system that can perform a wide range of computations.
the brain is a complex, dynamic, adaptive system that can change in response to experience.
